title: Meditation comfort shawl
subtitle: A large rectangle in chunky weight with alternating dc and treble columns, designed for sitting meditation
excerpt: This large rectangular shawl measures 170 cm wide by 70 cm deep in chunky weight yarn on a 6 mm hook. The stitch pattern alternates columns of double crochet and treble across each row, producing a textured surface with good body. The generous dimensions make it suitable for wrapping fully around the shoulders while seated. Suitable for crocheters who know both double crochet and treble.
sourceNotes: Original pattern synthesised for Homemade. Alternating dc and treble column fabric is a widely used texture technique with no single source.
heroPrompt: A large chunky crochet rectangle in warm rust-brown chunky yarn folded loosely on a wooden bench in a sparse room with good natural light, showing the alternating column texture across the width.

glossaryTerms.definition: A stitch pattern where double crochet and treble stitches alternate across every row. Because each stitch is worked into the same type of stitch in the row below, vertical columns of dc and tr appear across the fabric surface.

glossaryTerms.term: Turning chain for mixed stitch rows
glossaryTerms.definition: When a row begins with a dc column, ch 1 (does not count as a stitch) and work the first dc into the first stitch. When a row begins with a treble column, ch 3 (counts as the first tr). Whichever applies, the turning chain type must match the stitch it replaces.

content.text: This shawl uses a
dc-treble column

pattern throughout: each stitch in a row sits directly above the same stitch type in the row below. The result is a series of vertical raised columns across the fabric, which gives more texture and structure than plain treble alone. The wrap is large at 170 x 70 cm, designed to cover both shoulders and the lap when seated.
Because the rows contain both dc and tr, the
turning chain

pattern is consistent: the foundation chain sets the width and every subsequent row is identical. The stitch multiple is 2 (one dc plus one tr), so the stitch count must be even. A count of 204 gives 170 cm at the stated gauge.

attrs.title: Materials
attrs.body: Approximately 700 g chunky-weight yarn. A 6 mm crochet hook (US J/10). Tapestry needle. Craft scissors. Tape measure. Optional: blocking mat.

content.text: Gauge

12 sts x 8 rows = 10 x 10 cm in chunky yarn with a 6 mm hook, measured over the dc-treble column pattern. Work a swatch of 18 stitches and 12 rows; measure the central 10 x 10 cm area. At this weight, one stitch per 10 cm changes the finished width by about 14 cm.
Stitches used
chain (ch): UK and US shared.
slip stitch (sl st): UK and US shared.
double crochet (dc): UK; the same move as US "single crochet" (sc).
treble (tr): UK; the same move as US "double crochet" (dc).
Pattern

The wrap is worked flat in rows. Every row follows the same sequence: dc into each dc column, tr into each tr column. The first stitch of every row is always a dc (the dc column is on the left edge when viewed from the right side on odd rows).
Foundation chain
Ch 206. (204 working chains for 102 dc and 102 tr stitches, plus 2 turning chains.)
Row 1 (right side)
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). *1 dc in next ch. 1 tr in next ch*; repeat from * to * across. Turn. (102 dc, 102 tr = 204 sts)
Row 2
Ch 1 (does not count as a stitch). *1 dc in the next dc. 1 tr in the next tr*; repeat from * to * across. Turn. (204 sts)
Rows 3 to 56
Repeat Row 2 on every row. After Row 56 the wrap measures approximately 170 x 70 cm. Fasten off.

attrs.title: Keeping the columns aligned
attrs.body: The most common error in this stitch is working a dc into a tr or a tr into a dc, which breaks the column lines. After the first few rows, look down the fabric: each dc should sit directly above a dc and each tr above a tr. If the columns look diagonal, check the last row and correct before continuing.

content.text: Finishing

Fasten off and weave in all ends securely. Chunky yarn has a thick ply that can pull loose if the ends are only woven in one direction: pass the tapestry needle through at least four stitches, then double back for two stitches before trimming. Block lightly by laying flat, covering with a damp cloth, and leaving until dry.
Care
Handwash in cool water with a gentle wool wash. Press out excess water gently and lay flat to dry. Do not tumble-dry or hang while wet.
What to try next

Add a simple dc border around all four edges for a firmer selvedge. Work the same column pattern in DK on a 4 mm hook for a lighter version. A version in two contrasting colours, changing colour every 10 rows, gives horizontal stripes across the column texture.
